mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2% (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces earnings visibility and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage points over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls by >0.5pp over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by >0.5pp over two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed 12-month averages (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate higher corporate pricing power.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE is below 4% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).
